text: dsh-video-vision 是面向 DSH 的视频理解插件，通过注册五个工具，把本地视频、直链或 B 站视频转成可供模型查看和检索的画面与文本。它能先读取媒体元数据和阅读计划，再生成带时间码的分镜图、对指定片段放大、输出整片文字地图，或将讲课、幻灯片和录屏整理成带时间戳的文本。分镜会关联画面、切点、字幕和音频信息，文本阅读可利用 OCR 和已有字幕。适合分析视频内容、查找片段和整理课程材料；需要 ffmpeg，OCR 与语音识别引擎按需配置。

dsh-video-vision adds five video tools to DSH: metadata, timestamped storyboards, interval zoom, text maps, and timestamped lecture or screen recording text. It uses subtitles and OCR to help review footage and organize course material. ffmpeg is required; OCR and speech engines are optional.
我想让 DSH 帮我快速看一段视频并标出关键画面。
能不能把视频里的幻灯片和讲课内容整理成可搜索的文字？
想知道一个视频文件的时长、分辨率和音轨情况。
我想只看视频某个时间段的细节，不必重新分析整条片子。
让 DSH 把整段视频先做成不带图片的文字概览。
手上只有 B 站视频链接，想直接提取画面和字幕。
I need a timestamped text transcript of a lecture or screen recording.
Can I get a contact sheet that shows the important moments in a video?
I want to inspect one short interval in more visual detail.
dsh-video-vision 的功能「视频分镜」：为视频或选定时间窗生成一张分镜图，并附带逐格时间码和文本索引。调用 video_storyboard，可调整细节级别、格数和时间范围。
dsh-video-vision 的功能「视频放大」：针对一个短时间窗提取更清晰的画面格，便于检查字幕、动作或画面细节。调用 video_zoom 并提供视频和起止时间。
dsh-video-vision 的功能「视频文字阅读」：将讲课、幻灯片或录屏整理为带时间戳的文本，可结合视频字幕和 OCR 识别画面文字。调用 video_read 并传入视频文件。
dsh-video-vision 的功能「整片文字地图」：把视频分成时间窗口并输出文本概览，帮助决定值得进一步查看的片段，不返回分镜图片。调用 video_outline 并指定视频。
dsh-video-vision 使用前须知：运行视频分析需要系统可找到 ffmpeg；文字识别和语音转写则需另行提供可用引擎或命令。见 src/index.js:55-66、src/tools.js:23-30。

dsh-video-vision README · dsh-video-vision：**中文** · [English](README.en.md)

看画面，而不是听人转述视频。每次调用给出一张**可寻址的分镜图**（storyboard
grid），为 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 的视觉能力调优。可直接替换
`dsh-video-storyboard` / `dsh-video-understand` —— 三个工具名与参数形状跟它们一样，
另加两个它们没有的答案：一张整条片子的文本地图，什么都不画；一份给「有声无画面」
的文件的转录。

```
video_probe      元数据 + 阅读计划，不解码画面
video_outline    整条片子读成一行行文本 —— 0 张图、0 个视觉 token
video_storyboard 一张分镜图 + 逐格绑定时间码的文本索引
video_zoom       对一个短窗口放大看，1-9 格

dsh-video-vision README · dsh-video-vision：画面路径是给电影、体育、游戏，任何「画面本身就是内容」的片子用的。当内容就是屏幕
上的字时，`video_read` 直接赢：一堂两小时的课变成 7.7k 字的 `[mm:ss] 文本`，
外加十一道例题的目录，模型可以引用、检索、改写成笔记 —— 而在那个尺度上，一张
1024 token 的分镜图是读不出字的。两小时的片子 87 秒，95 秒带字幕的片段 5.6 秒，
36 秒的片段 1.3 秒。

> 每一项设计决定背后的实测数据见 [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md)；
> 逐片段实测、误差说明与复现方式见 [docs/EVIDENCE.md](docs/EVIDENCE.md)。

dsh-video-vision README · dsh-video-vision：

D 片段：六张只有文字块不同的卡片，六格 / 359 token，每一条项目符号都清晰可读。
G 片段：九格 + 音频带 —— 青色包络、橙色说话区间、黄色切点刻度。一张图 542 token。

video_zoom 看一个 1 秒叠化：前、过渡中、后，三格大图。
---

dsh-video-vision README · 好在哪：**能看见「亮度相同」的切点。** 每个画面被压成 12x7 的**亮度块 + 色度块**，
一次 ffmpeg 解码同时算出。两个镜头亮度几乎一样、只是调色不同时，只看得见亮度的
检测器会认为「什么都没发生」，这里不会。跳变被分成五类：`cut`（真切）、
`partial`（画面的一部分被新内容替换）、`overlay`（字幕/贴图出现）、`light`（开灯）、
`noise`；只有前两类会变成切点。

**没有切点的幻灯片，也能一张卡一格。** 六张只换正文的标题卡，画面只有 1–6% 在动
——低于「字幕换行也算切」的门槛——所以扫描把它判成「文字运动」，再由这些变动点
直接切格子：六张卡、六格，页头仍然诚实地写着 `0 cuts`。

**闪光和转场不算新镜头。** 单帧白闪会在 3 帧内恢复原画面，直接丢弃；叠化
（dissolve）被识别为**瞬态**——一段变化的平台期，之后必须安静下来——因此只产生
一个边界，而不是一串碎镜头；而缓慢摇镜不会产生任何边界。

dsh-video-vision README · 好在哪：**图按「每格」定尺寸，不按「整张」定。** 宿主按面积计费
（`tokens = gridH*(gridW+1)+2`，上限 1024）。1.25 Mpx 的图里放 10 格和放 4 格
**同价**，所以预算用来换「更多时刻、更小的格」，直到格子看不清为止：
6 格约 350 token，20 格约 1000 token，内容少的片子自然就便宜。

**格子是挣来的，不是平均分的。** 每个镜头保底一格；额外格子只给「时长够长」且
「存在一帧与已选帧的距离超过同图阈值 2.5 倍」的镜头。静态口播永远拿不到第二格，
30 秒摇镜会分到 4 格。

**没有切点的长段，按「变化」给格。** 讲课、录屏、写板书：十一分钟只有一个镜头，
而要看懂恰恰靠「每分钟多出了什么」。超过 90 秒的段，判据从「这两张图差多远」换成
「画面里有没有新的东西」——同样在 12×7 的块网格上算，一次变化一格，最多每 30 秒
一格、整段不超过 24 格。19 分钟的时间窗从 4 格变成 22 格，分镜图预算仍是
1024 token。

dsh-video-vision README · 好在哪：**解码是批量的。** 6 格共用**一个** ffmpeg 进程（多个输入、各自输出），并发 3 个
进程——一张 20 格的图只启动 2-4 次进程，而不是 60 次。

**最便宜的一眼，是不画任何东西。** `video_outline` 把整条片子切成等长窗口，用
一行行文本回答——切点数、说话占比、一条八格强度条、一个标签——再点出三个值得打开
的窗口，以及拿来打开它们的确切 `start`/`end`。它花 **0 个视觉 token**，短片
不到一秒：它的用处是决定**哪里**值得花一张图，而这恰恰是分镜图对一堂两小时的课
说不了的事。

**一格永远不会糊成一条。** 以前 `auto` 不看来料多大，都往一张 1.76 Mpx 的图里
塞 28 格，于是一条 4K 片子拿到的是 28 张 77 px 高的画。现在这张图保留同样的预算，
花在更少、更大的格子上——任何一格不低于原片高度的五分之一：720p 28 格、
1080p 21 格、1440p 11 格、4K 5 格——仍是约 1024 token；触到这条底线时，结果里会
写明。

dsh-video-vision README · 好在哪：**过了十分钟，只读关键帧。** 长片在关键帧至少相隔一秒时按关键帧分析：一堂两小时
的课快 **2.7 倍**，并在结果里说明「再缩短会漏掉什么」，以及用
`DSH_SCAN_KEYFRAMES=off` 退回逐帧。短窗口和短文件仍然逐帧解码，和以前一样。

**结果里不写废话。** 阅读说明放在工具描述里（属于可缓存的 prompt 前缀，只付一次），
结果本身只包含索引和那张图。`textOnly` + `cellRange` 可以零图像成本翻页，
重复调用命中缓存。

---

dsh-video-vision README · 数据：文本地图这一项是构造上就等于零的：`video_outline` 一张图都不返回，所以可以在
为任何一张图付钱之前，先把整条片子过一遍。

对一部 **13 分钟**的片子，一次调用给**一张**图：28 格、每格 331x186、1024 token、
6.2 秒，连同索引共约 1353 token 的上下文。完整表格在 EVIDENCE.md。

弱项写在上面那个文件里，不四舍五入：1 秒叠化会被判成一次渐变边界，而标准答案
认为该片段「没有切点」，所以这里记一次误报；语料里还有两个片段整帧换画面
（章节卡、音乐段落），会被判成切点。真实视频的抽检与实际可读性截图：
[docs/REAL-WORLD.md](docs/REAL-WORLD.md)。

dsh-video-vision README · 安装：插件**零运行时依赖**。需要 `ffmpeg`；有 `ffprobe` 时用它，没有就从
`ffmpeg -i` 的输出里解析元数据。

```bash

dsh-video-vision README · 从 registry 装：在 DSH profile 目录里执行：npm i dsh-video-vision
npx dsh-video-vision-install         # 改 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop，然后重启 DSH
section: 从 registry 装：在 DSH profile 目录里执行

text:
dsh-video-vision README · 或者直接用一份 checkout，不必先装：cd /path/to/dsh-video-vision
node bin/install.mjs                 # 改 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop，然后重启 DSH
node bin/install.mjs --dry-run       # 只打印要改什么，不动文件
node bin/install.mjs --remove        # 卸载
```

脚本手工做完了 `pnpm install` 本来会做的三件事：往 profile 的 `dependencies` 里写
`"dsh-video-vision": "link:<绝对路径>"`、把包名加进 `dsh.profile.bundles`、把包
**目录联接（junction）**到 profile 的 `node_modules`。可重复执行；`--copy` 改成
复制一份快照而不是链接。无论哪种方式，装完都要**重启应用**：包内的
`cordis.patch.yml` 在启动时把插件插入 harness 树，五个工具才会出现。
section: 或者直接用一份 checkout，不必先装

text:
dsh-video-vision README · ffmpeg 查找顺序：查找顺序（先命中先用）：`$DSH_FFMPEG_PATH` → `$DSH_VIDEO_FFMPEG` →
`$FFMPEG_PATH` → 包内 `vendor/bin` → node_modules 里的 `ffmpeg-static` /
`@ffmpeg-installer` → WinGet Links → `C:\ffmpeg\bin` → scoop shims →
npm roaming → `/usr/local/bin` → `~/.dsh/dsh-runtimes/*/` 里的
`imageio-ffmpeg` wheel → `PATH` 上的 `ffmpeg`。
`$DSH_FFPROBE_PATH` / `$FFPROBE_PATH` 对 ffprobe 做同样的事。

ffmpeg 4.x 以上都能用：抽帧器会先问一次二进制自己的版本，5.1 及以后用
`-fps_mode passthrough`，更老的用 `-vsync 0`，万一被拒就换另一种拼法重试一次。

一条命令端到端验一台机器（不需要现成视频，它会自己生成一个）：

dsh-video-vision README · ffmpeg 查找顺序：```bash
node bin/selfcheck.mjs --smoke          # 21 项检查，自己生成素材
node bin/selfcheck.mjs --smoke --host   # 40 项：校验全部五个工具，对着已安装的
                                        # Harness 自己的 schema 引擎
node --test test/                       # 339 个单元测试，不联网，临时目录隔离

dsh-video-vision README · ffmpeg 查找顺序：`--host` 跑的是 `ctx.tools.register` 真正执行的断言，然后逐个工具真调用一次，
再按运行时的规则校验返回值。要用 Electron 的 node 跑（`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`），
普通 node 读不进 `app.asar`。这不是形式主义：工具如果返回 `{ text: {…} }` 而不是
`{ text: "…" }`，宿主会直接拒绝并报 `"value.text" must be a string`，本地一切
正常，直到有用户按下调用。

section: 先画一张图，这一步不花钱

text:
dsh-video-vision README · 先画一张图，这一步不花钱：每一行是一个窗口：切点数、这个窗口里说话占多少、一条强度条（八格，高度由切点、
运动、说话量与响事件决定），以及最多两个标签——`dark`、`static`、`quiet`、
`busy`、`talk`。`watch first` 先按「屏幕上变化多少」排，再按「说了多少」排；
`next` 把这些数字直接带进真正去开窗口的那次调用。没有任何东西被解码两遍：
同一次分析也供所选窗口的分镜图使用。

| 参数 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | 文件路径、直链，或 B站 链接 |
| `windows` | 4–60 个等长切片（默认 24） |
| `top` | `watch first` 里点几个窗口（1–8，默认 3） |
section: 先画一张图，这一步不花钱

text:
dsh-video-vision README · 一张分镜图：```
video_storyboard input:"C:\clips\pv.mp4"
```

```
pv.mp4 · 0:00:40.00 · 1280x720 · 30fps · 9 cuts · median shot 4.00s
sheet 1 · 2x5 grid · 942x1328 · 10 cells · window 00:00.00-00:40.00
cols: cell · pos · span · (cuts) · frame@
1 r1c1 00:00.00-00:04.00 @00:01.98

图片在同一个工具结果里返回。`r2c1` = 从上往下第 2 行、从左往右第 1 列；格子左上角
烧进去的数字就是格号。

dsh-video-vision README · 一张分镜图：| 参数 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | 文件路径，或 ffmpeg 能直接抓取的 `http(s)` 媒体地址 |
| `start` / `end` / `duration` | 只看一个窗口 |
| `detail` | `low`（≤6 格）· `auto`（≤20，默认）· `high`（≤28） |
| `cells` | 强制格数（1-24） |
| `pick` | `sharp`（默认）/ `middle` |
| `dedupe` | `shots`（默认）只合并同一镜头内的重复画面 · `global` 连跨切点的重复也合并 |
| `textOnly` | 只返回文本索引：不取图、不解码 |
| `cellRange` | 配合 `textOnly`，列出第 a 到第 b 格 |

`video_zoom` 支持同样的窗口参数，外加 `cells`（1-9）与 `at`；只有 1 格时返回
原分辨率单帧。

dsh-video-vision README · 哪些格子需要放大：分镜拼得密，每格就小，一行字幕或一行代码会缩成灰带，而那一格整体看着仍然是好画面。
索引会直接说，不用你猜：

```
cols: cell · pos · span · (cuts) · frame@ · zoom
zoom: 3/22 cells carry detail finer than the sheet can show at 6.4x — cells 4, 9, 17 are marked, the rest read fine as they are
4  r2c1 00:12.00-00:28.00 @00:19.80 zoom
```

测量是把每格按格大小的两倍解一次再比对，所以读图成本不变、也不多花图像 token。
空帧、纯色卡片、黑边这类没有细节的格子不会被标记；如果每一格都太小，索引只说一次，
并建议用 `detail:"low"` 换更大的格子。`DSH_VIDEO_ZOOM_MARKERS=0` 可以关掉。

dsh-video-vision README · 读一堂课：```
video_read input:"C:\clips\lecture.mp4"
```

```

dsh-video-vision README · outline：00:45 1.1
17:20 例题3
41:05 例题5
56:16 例题6
74:00 例题8

[00:45–01:44] 1.1 归纳证明 事实上，数学归纳法的使用是很灵活的…
[17:20–18:54] 例题 3 ．A、B 二人玩如下游戏：初始时有两堆硬币，各 2ⁿ 个…
```

长片只解**关键帧**（`-skip_frame nokey`），按画面变化聚类，每类只 OCR 一次幻灯片
区域，再把说的是同一件事的屏合并。几乎一样的幻灯片从两端往中间压：OCR 噪声让精确
比对失效，所以「是不是同一屏」用字符二元组相似度来判。
video_read input:"C:\clips\lecture.mp4" out:"C:\notes\lecture.srt"
```

短片走抽样而不是关键帧：十五分钟以内每 1.2 秒解一帧，只解一遍，再用 0.4% 的画面
变化做闸门，通过的那些帧就是 OCR 真正读的帧——所以一个固定版式、只有字幕在变的
片子，是一行字一屏，而不是整条片子一屏。更长的片子仍走关键帧那条路，那里贵的是
解码，不是 OCR。

dsh-video-vision README · outline：丢掉的是录屏软件，不是课：标签栏是贴着上边缘的短行，状态栏是贴着下边缘的短行，
聊天面板是一屏全是极短的行，老师手写的那些帧只会 OCR 成一堆两个字的碎片、没有
一句完整的话。这几个判据都是几何位置，跟是哪个软件录的无关。

实测一条 1:59:54、2560x1440 的真实课程：**87 秒**解完 975 个关键帧 →
**53 屏 → 7 663 字**，十一道例题全在目录里。同一条片子走 `video_storyboard` 要
163 秒，返回的是一张 1024 token 的分镜图，上面的幻灯片文字看不清。15 分钟窗口
**16 秒**读完；36 秒短片 **1.3 秒**。

dsh-video-vision README · 语音转文字（自带引擎时）：如果把 `DSH_ASR_CMD` 指向一个你信得过的引擎，`video_storyboard` 和
`video_read` 会把**说的话**也引出来，不只是字：

```
set DSH_ASR_CMD=C:\python\python.exe F:\asr\engine.py --model small {wav} {out}
```

这一段的音频抽一次（16 kHz 单声道），跑你的命令，解析它写到 `{out}`（或直接打到
stdout）的 SRT。每句话挂在「中点落在哪一格」的格子上，所以一句只引一次。有字幕轨
时永远优先用字幕：那是人写的，而且不用解码。

text:
dsh-video-vision README · 语音转文字（自带引擎时）：**长音频先切块。** 把一小时、230 MB 的 wav 整个丢给识别器，换来的往往不是转录而是
OOM，所以超过 `DSH_ASR_CHUNK_SECONDS`（45）的窗口会被切开：先只做一遍解码，专门
听停顿；然后每个 45 秒的目标点往回退到最近的静音中点，且至少退到块内
`DSH_ASR_CHUNK_MIN`（12）秒处——一刀落在停顿里，而不是落在一个词中间。末尾剩下
的一点会并进前一块。切块以 `DSH_ASR_PARALLEL`（2）并行抽取与转写，时间戳再按块
平移回去，让一句话的时间就是文件里的时间；被切点分到两边、重复了一遍的那句会合并
成一句。停顿的门限是 `DSH_ASR_SILENCE_DB`（−32 dB）与 `DSH_ASR_SILENCE_MIN`
（0.35 秒）；`DSH_ASR_CHUNK_SECONDS=0` 可以关掉切块，交给想要整条文件的引擎。

某一块失败不会把整份转录拖走：其余的都保留，返回的原因会说清有几块、在哪——
`1 of 3 audio chunk(s) failed — chunk at 01:30: …`。

dsh-video-vision README · 语音转文字（自带引擎时）：**故意不内置模型**：这个包是 600 KB 代码、零依赖，而准度在模型里（tiny 75 MB、
small 484 MB、medium 1.5 GB）。同一段两分钟的真实课堂录音、16 线程实测：

| 引擎 | 转录耗时 | 两小时外推 | 读出来的样子 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tiny` | 2.5 s | 约 2.5 分钟 | 乱：把「选法」听成「選抜」，把「枚举」听成「按摩機束」 |
| `small` | 15.5 s | 约 15 分钟 | 可读，输出繁体，「递推」听成「地规」 |

本机自带的离线识别也试过并放弃：`System.Speech` 中文把同一分钟变成一行 60 字、
置信度 **1.7 %** 的乱码——那种「有 ASR」比没有更糟，所以这里是钩子而不是功能。

分工因此是：课件、录屏走 `video_read`（两小时 87–112 秒），纯语音走 ASR，
两者都要时先读字，再对关心的那一段传 `start`/`end` 跑 ASR。

**识别器的两类毛病由客户端负责**，因为每个引擎都有，而每个调用方都会各自做错：

text:
dsh-video-vision README · 语音转文字（自带引擎时）：- **音乐不是人声。** 让识别器转一段纯音乐，它不会交白卷——它会编一句话，再给它
  一个很长的时间段。一段 90 秒的 PV 上编出了 29 秒的假台词，而格子是按时间重叠
  引用的，于是同一句垃圾被贴到五张卡上。所以：只剩标点的句子、以及超过 8 秒且
  每秒不足 0.8 个字（真人说话是 2–6）的句子会被丢掉，并且**把丢了几条写进清单**
  （`2 suspect line(s) dropped`）——没人能审计的过滤器，和一个坏掉的识别器看不出
  区别。
- **术语是你的，不是互联网的。** `递推` 会听成 `地规`，`阶乘` 会听成 `階層`。
  把更正和命令一起写进 `~/.dsh/asr.json`：

```json
  {
    "cmd": "C:\\python\\python.exe F:\\asr\\engine.py --model small {wav} {out}",
    "terms": { "地规": "递推", "階層": "阶乘" }
  }

每个条目都在**两种字形**下各试一次（一堂课里实际会出现约 50 对简繁），因为

**格子边界会挪到静音处。** 台词本来就知道句子在哪结束，所以离静音中点 1.5 秒以内
的边界会被移过去，而不是把一张卡切在某个字的第十个百分之一秒上；挪动之后任何格子
都不短于 0.3 秒。

（`[{start,end,text}]`，或 whisper 系工具输出的 `{"segments":[…]}`），**优先于**

dsh-video-vision README · 做不到什么：- **不内置语音识别。** 只有文件自带字幕轨，或者你按上面的方式配了 `DSH_ASR_CMD`
  时，才会转录说话。两者都没有时，仍然给你音频摘要：说话占比、响度、静音、起音。
  长窗口会切块，但模型是你自己的：这个包从不下载模型。
- **OCR 要用三种引擎之一。** Windows 自带的那个（`Windows.Media.Ocr`）是内建的；
  Linux 和 macOS 用 `PATH` 上的 `tesseract`；`DSH_OCR_CMD` 指向任何「吃一张
  图、吐几行字」的引擎。三种都没有时工具直说——`DSH_OCR_BACKEND=off` 强制给出
  这个答案，而 `video_outline` 或 `video_storyboard` 照样能用，因为它们都不读字。
- **只认 B站，而且只拿它愿意给的清晰度。** B站 链接走公开接口解析，也就是说没有
  cookie（`DSH_BILIBILI_COOKIE`）就只有 720P；没有 `yt-dlp`，其它站点仍然要先
  下载成文件。付费内容和会员专享读不了。
- **切点是检测出来的，不是理解出来的。** 快速甩镜和硬切在 96x54 的网格里可能相似，
  分类器在「变化很局部」时倾向于判「不是切点」。
- **它不是播放器。** 一次调用 = 一张最多 28 个瞬间的静态图。

Look at a video instead of being told about one: **one addressable storyboard
grid per view**, tuned for `deepseek-v4.1-flash` vision. Drop-in replacement for
`dsh-video-storyboard` / `dsh-video-understand` — the same three tool names and
argument shapes as those, plus two answers they do not have: a text map of the

dsh-video-vision README · dsh-video-vision：```
video_probe       metadata + a reading plan, no frames decoded
video_outline     the whole file as rows of text — 0 images, 0 vision tokens
video_storyboard  one contact sheet + a text index binding every cell to a timecode
video_zoom        1-9 large cells over a short window

dsh-video-vision README · dsh-video-vision：Picture paths are for film, sport, gameplay, anything where the picture *is* the
content. When the content is text on the screen, `video_read` wins outright: a
two-hour lecture becomes 7.7k characters of `[mm:ss] text` plus an outline of its
eleven worked examples, which the model can quote, search and rewrite into notes —
where a 1024-token contact sheet is unreadable at that size. It costs 87 s for two
hours of video, 5.6 s for a 95-second subtitled clip, and 1.3 s for a 36-second one.

dsh-video-vision README · dsh-video-vision：

Clip D: six slides that differ only in their text block. Six cells, 359 vision tokens, every bullet readable.
Clip G: nine cells plus an audio band — teal envelope, orange speech spans, yellow cut ticks. One image, 542 tokens.

video_zoom over a 1 s crossfade: before, mid-transition, after — three cells at full width.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**It sees cuts a luma-only detector cannot.** Every frame is reduced to a 12x7
grid of luma *and* chroma block means in a single ffmpeg pass, so a cut between
two shots of identical brightness — a day scene to a differently graded day
scene — is still a cut. Jumps are then classified five ways: `cut`, `partial`
(part of the frame replaced by bigger content), `overlay` (a caption appearing),
`light` (a lamp switching on) and `noise`; only the first two become cuts.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**A deck with no cuts still gets a cell per card.** Six title cards that change
only their body text move 1–6 % of the picture — below the bar that would make a
caption swap a shot — so the scan calls the clip text motion instead, and the
marks become the cell boundaries: six cards, six cells, with `0 cuts` still
reported honestly in the header.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**Flashes and fades are not shots.** A one-frame white flash restores the
picture within three frames and is rejected; a dissolve is recognised as a
*transient* — a plateau of change that stops afterwards — so it yields one
boundary instead of a burst of tiny shots, while a slow pan yields none.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**The sheet is sized per cell, not per sheet.** The host bills an image by area
(`tokens = gridH*(gridW+1)+2`, 1024 cap). Ten cells in a 1.25 Mpx sheet cost
exactly what four cost, so the budget buys *more moments at smaller cells* until
cells stop being legible — six cells get ~350 tokens, twenty get ~1000, and a
cheap clip stays cheap.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**Cells are earned, not evenly spaced.** One cell per shot is the floor; extra
cells go only to shots that are long enough *and* have a frame 2.5x further from
every chosen frame than the "same picture" threshold. A static talking head
never earns a second cell; a 30 s pan spreads over four.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**A cutless stretch is planned by what changed inside it.** A lecture, a screen
share, a board being written on: one shot for eleven minutes, and the whole point
is what appeared minute by minute. Past 90 s the planner switches question — from
"how far apart are these pictures" to "did any part of the frame gain something
new" — measured on the same 12×7 block grid, one cell per change, 30 s apart at
most, capped at 24. A 19-minute window goes from four cells to twenty-two at the
same 1 024-token budget.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**Decoding is batched.** Six cell extractions share one ffmpeg process (several
inputs, one output each), three processes in flight — a 20-cell sheet costs 2-4
process launches instead of 60.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**The cheapest look is a look at nothing.** `video_outline` cuts the file into
equal windows and answers in rows — cuts, speech share, an eight-character
intensity bar, a tag — then names the three windows worth opening and the exact
`start`/`end` to open them with. It costs **zero vision tokens** and under a
second for a short clip: the point is to decide *where* to spend a sheet, which
is the one thing a contact sheet cannot tell you about a two-hour lecture.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**A cell is never a smear.** `auto` used to fill a 1.76 Mpx sheet with 28 cells
whatever the source size, so a 4K file got 28 pictures of 77 px tall. The sheet
keeps its budget and now spends it on fewer, bigger cells — no cell smaller than
a fifth of the source height: 720p 28, 1080p 21, 1440p 11, 4K 5 — at the same
~1 024 tokens, and it says so when the rail binds.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**Ten minutes in, it reads the keyframes.** A long file is analysed on its
keyframes when they are at least a second apart: 2.7× faster on a two-hour
lecture, with a note naming what a shorter change would hide and
`DSH_SCAN_KEYFRAMES=off` to undo it. Short windows and short files decode every
frame exactly as before.

dsh-video-vision README · Why it is better：**No prose in results.** Reading instructions live in the tool description,
which sits in the cached prompt prefix and is paid once; the result itself is
only the index and the image. `textOnly` + `cellRange` pages a long film at zero
image cost, and repeat calls are cached.

On a **13-minute** film one call returns **one** image: 28 cells at 331x186,
1 024 tokens, 6.2 s, ~1 353 tokens of context including the index. Full table
in EVIDENCE.md.

dsh-video-vision README · Numbers：Where this plugin is weak is stated there rather than rounded away: a 1 s
crossfade is reported as one dissolve boundary and scored as a false positive
against a ground truth that calls it zero cuts, and two clips in the corpus
change their whole frame between sections, so they read as cuts. Real-world spot
checks with screenshots of what was actually readable:
[docs/REAL-WORLD.md](docs/REAL-WORLD.md).

`$FFMPEG_PATH`, the package's own `vendor/bin`, `ffmpeg-static` /
`@ffmpeg-installer` in node_modules, WinGet Links, `C:\ffmpeg\bin`, scoop shims,
the npm roaming prefix, `/usr/local/bin`, an `imageio-ffmpeg` wheel inside
`~/.dsh/dsh-runtimes/*/`, then plain `ffmpeg` on `PATH`.
`$DSH_FFPROBE_PATH` / `$FFPROBE_PATH` do the same for ffprobe.

dsh-video-vision README · ffmpeg：Any ffmpeg from 4.x up works: the frame reader asks the binary for its version
once and uses `-fps_mode passthrough` (5.1 and later) or `-vsync 0` (older),
retrying with the other spelling if the build rejects the first.

Verify a machine end to end (no video needed — it builds one):

dsh-video-vision README · ffmpeg：```bash
node bin/selfcheck.mjs --smoke          # 21 checks, builds its own clip
node bin/selfcheck.mjs --smoke --host   # 40 checks: validates all five tools against the
                                        # installed Harness's schema engine
node --test test/                       # 339 tests, no network, hermetic temp dirs

dsh-video-vision README · ffmpeg：`--host` runs the exact assertions `ctx.tools.register` runs, then calls every
tool once and validates the result the way the runtime does. Run it with
Electron's node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`) — plain node cannot read inside
`app.asar`. This is not ceremony: a tool that returns `{ text: {…} }` instead of
`{ text: "…" }` is rejected by the host with `"value.text" must be a string`,
and nothing local notices until a user calls it.

section: Map it first — it costs nothing

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Map it first — it costs nothing：(That is an untouched run over this package's own 57-second promo clip: 1.9 s,
no image, no vision tokens.)
section: Map it first — it costs nothing

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Map it first — it costs nothing：Each row is one window: cuts, the share of it that is speech, an intensity bar
(eight slices, height = cuts, motion, speech and loud events), and at most two
tags — `dark`, `static`, `text`, `quiet`, `busy`, `talk`. `static` and `text`
are not the same answer: a clip whose frame barely moves while its captions keep
swapping is tagged `text`, and the answer says so in a `note:` and points at
`video_read` instead of leaving a model to conclude the file is empty.
`watch first` ranks by how much changes on screen first and how much is said
second; `next` carries those numbers into the call that actually opens a window.
Nothing is decoded twice: the same analysis pass serves the storyboard of the
chosen window.
section: Map it first — it costs nothing

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Map it first — it costs nothing：| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | file path, direct URL, or B站 link |
| `windows` | 4–60 equal slices (default 24) |
| `top` | how many windows to name in `watch first` (1–8, default 3) |

sheet 1 · 2x5 grid · 942x1328 · 10 cells · window 00:00.00-00:40.00

The image arrives in the same tool result. `r2c1` is row 2, column 1 from the

dsh-video-vision README · One sheet of pictures：| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | file path, or a direct `http(s)` URL that ffmpeg can fetch |
| `start` / `end` / `duration` | read one window instead of the whole file |
| `detail` | `low` (≤6 cells) · `auto` (≤20, default) · `high` (≤28) |

dsh-video-vision README · One sheet of pictures：`video_zoom` takes the same window arguments plus `cells` (1–9) and `at`; a
single cell is returned at full resolution.

dsh-video-vision README · Which cells need a closer look：A dense sheet is small per cell, so a subtitle line or a line of code can shrink
into a smear while the cell still looks like a perfectly good picture. The index
tells you instead of leaving you to guess:

```
cols: cell · pos · span · (cuts) · frame@ · zoom
zoom: 3/22 cells carry detail finer than the sheet can show at 6.4x — cells 4, 9, 17 are marked, the rest read fine as they are
4  r2c1 00:12.00-00:28.00 @00:19.80 zoom
```
section: Which cells need a closer look

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Which cells need a closer look：Each cell is decoded at twice the cell size for the measurement, so this costs
nothing extra to read and adds no image tokens. Cells with no fine detail — a
black frame, a flat title card, letterbox bars — are never marked; when every
cell is too small the line says so once and suggests `detail:"low"` for bigger
cells. `DSH_VIDEO_ZOOM_MARKERS=0` turns it off.
section: Which cells need a closer look

For a long video it decodes **only keyframes** (`-skip_frame nokey`), clusters
them by picture change, OCRs the slide area of each cluster once, then merges
screens that say the same thing. Near-identical slides are collapsed from both ends: OCR noise
video_read input:"C:\clips\lecture.mp4" out:"C:\notes\lecture.srt"
```

dsh-video-vision README · outline：Short videos are read by sampling instead of by keyframe: under fifteen minutes
one frame every 1.2 s is decoded once, gated on a 0.4 % picture change, and the
frames that pass are the exact frames OCR reads — so a fixed layout whose only
change is the subtitle line yields one screen per line, not one screen for the
whole clip. Longer videos keep the keyframe path, where decoding, not OCR, is the
cost.

dsh-video-vision README · outline：What gets thrown away is the recorder, not the lecture: a tab strip is a short
line near the top edge, a status bar is a short line at the bottom, a chat panel
is a screen made of very short lines, and a frame where the teacher is writing
by hand OCRs into a pile of two-character stubs with no sentence in it. Those
tests are geometric, so they work whatever app the recording came from.

dsh-video-vision README · outline：Measured on a real 1:59:54 lecture at 2560x1440: **87 s** for 975 keyframes →
**53 screens → 7 663 characters**, with all eleven worked examples in the
outline. The same file through `video_storyboard` takes 163 s and returns one
1 024-token sheet whose slide text is unreadable. A 15-minute window reads in
**16 s**; a 36-second clip in **1.3 s**.

dsh-video-vision README · outline：| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | file path, or a direct `http(s)` URL that ffmpeg can fetch |
| `start` / `end` | read one window only |
| `maxScreens` | cap on distinct screens read, 3–400 (default 400) |
| `out` | write the result: `.srt`/`.vtt` subtitle file, other extensions `[mm:ss]` text |
| `transcriptFile` | SRT/VTT/JSON you already have — tried before the engine, and the only way in for an audio-only file with no engine |

dsh-video-vision README · outline：Needs an OCR engine, and uses whichever it finds: the Windows one (built in, no
download, no model), `tesseract` on `PATH` anywhere, or `DSH_OCR_CMD` pointing
at an engine of your own (one image path in, lines out). `DSH_OCR_BACKEND` is
`windows` · `tesseract` · `off`, and `DSH_OCR_LANG` passes `-l` to
tesseract. With no engine at all the tool says so instead of pretending: the
Windows engine is probed for a recogniser language before it is used, so a
Windows Server (the engine is there, the language pack is not) falls back to
pictures rather than failing the read.

dsh-video-vision README · Reading from B站 without downloading：The CDN link is a signed mp4, so ffmpeg reads it in place. `video_probe` always did;
as of 1.3.2 `video_storyboard`, `video_zoom` and `video_read` do too, for clips up to
`DSH_BILIBILI_STREAM_MAX` seconds (default 300). Longer videos are downloaded once and
cached — a two-hour lecture streamed twice is more traffic than keeping it. Force either
behaviour with `DSH_BILIBILI_STREAM=1` (never download) or `=0` (always download).

dsh-video-vision README · Reading from B站 without downloading：Measured on a 57-second clip: storyboard 5.7 s streamed vs 1.9 s cached, `video_read`
8.3 s and 2 161 characters — and nothing written to disk.

**The playurl is cached in memory for ten minutes** (`DSH_BILIBILI_PLAY_TTL_MS`,
default 600 000). Asking probe, then storyboard, then read about one B站 file
otherwise resolves the same signed link three times; each answer stays valid for
hours, so the cache is keyed on
`bvid|cid|maxHeight|auth` and a hit is reported as `cached: true`.

dsh-video-vision README · Reading from B站 without downloading：**And the download cache has a budget**: `DSH_BILIBILI_CACHE_MB` (default 4096) and
`DSH_BILIBILI_CACHE_MAX` (default 24 videos). Least recently used goes first, the
file being written is never evicted, and each video's `.mp4`/`.json`/`.srt` leave
together.

dsh-video-vision README · Reading from B站 without downloading：**A link that is not one video gets the reason, not "unsupported":** a `bangumi/play/ep`
or `ss` link says which episode or season it is and that a p-segment of a season is
what this reads; `bangumi/media/md` is a whole work; a live room has no ending to
sample; a space or `/list/` link is a collection, so the answer names the collection
and asks for one video; `opus`/`read`/`t.bilibili.com` is a picture post with no
video in it.

dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：`video_storyboard` and `video_read` can quote what is being **said** as well as
what is written, if you point `DSH_ASR_CMD` at an engine you already trust:

```
set DSH_ASR_CMD=C:\python\python.exe F:\asr\engine.py --model small {wav} {out}
```
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：The window's audio is extracted once (16 kHz mono), your command runs, and the SRT
it writes to `{out}` — or prints on stdout — is parsed. Each line is quoted on the
cell that contains its midpoint, so nothing is repeated. A subtitle track, when
present, always wins: it was captioned by a human and costs no decode.
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：**Long audio is cut into chunks first.** Handing a recogniser one 230 MB hour-long
wav is how you get an OOM instead of a transcript, so a window longer than
`DSH_ASR_CHUNK_SECONDS` (45) is split: one decode pass only listens for pauses,
then each 45 s aim is walked back to the last silence midpoint at least
`DSH_ASR_CHUNK_MIN` (12 s) into the chunk, so a cut lands in a pause and not in a
word. A sliver at the end folds into the chunk before it. Chunks are extracted and
transcribed `DSH_ASR_PARALLEL` at a time (2), timestamps are shifted back per
chunk so a line's time is the file's time, and a line repeated on both sides of a
cut is merged once. Pause thresholds are `DSH_ASR_SILENCE_DB` (−32 dB) and
`DSH_ASR_SILENCE_MIN` (0.35 s); `DSH_ASR_CHUNK_SECONDS=0` turns chunking off for an
engine that wants the whole file.
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：A chunk that fails does not take the transcript with it: the rest is kept and the
returned reason says how many and where — `1 of 3 audio chunk(s) failed — chunk at
01:30: …`.

No engine is bundled, deliberately. This package is 600 KB of code with zero
dependencies, and the accuracy lives in the model (tiny 75 MB, small 484 MB,
medium 1.5 GB). Measured on two minutes of a real lecture on 16 threads:
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：| engine | transcript time | two hours, extrapolated | what comes out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tiny` | 2.5 s | ~2.5 min | garbled: `選抜` for 选法, `按摩機束` for 枚举 |
| `small` | 15.5 s | ~15 min | readable, Traditional output, `地规` for 递推 |

The host's own offline recogniser was tried and rejected: `System.Speech` zh-CN
turned the same minute into one 60-character line at **1.7 % confidence**. That is
worse than returning nothing, which is why this is a hook and not a feature.
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：So the split is: slides and screen recordings go through `video_read` (87–112 s
for two hours), speech-only material through ASR, and when you need both, read
first and run ASR on the window you care about by passing `start`/`end`.

**The client owns two of the recogniser's failure modes**, because every engine has
them and every caller would otherwise reinvent them badly:
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：- *Music is not speech.* Asked to transcribe an instrumental, a recogniser does
  not return nothing — it invents a sentence and gives it a long timestamp. On a
  90-second PV that produced a fake 29-second line, and since cells are quoted by
  time overlap the same garbage landed in five cards. Lines that are
  punctuation-only, or longer than 8 s at under 0.8 characters per second (real
  speech runs 2–6), are dropped; **the count is reported** in the manifest line as
  `2 suspect line(s) dropped`, because a filter nobody can audit is
  indistinguishable from a recogniser that stopped working.
- *The vocabulary is yours, not the internet's.* `递推` comes back `地规`, `阶乘`
  comes back `階層`. Put the corrections in `~/.dsh/asr.json` beside the command:
section: Speech, when you have an engine
Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：Each key is tried in **both scripts** (≈50 Simplified/Traditional pairs a
  lecture actually contains), because whisper transcribes Mandarin into
  Traditional: a key written `地规` has to match the `地規` that comes back, and
  before this it silently did nothing. Write the dictionary in the characters you
  think in; the other spelling works too.
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：**Cell boundaries move onto silence.** Dialogue already knows where its sentences
end, so a boundary within 1.5 s of a silence midpoint is moved there instead of
splitting a card an arbitrary tenth of a second into the next word. No card gets
shorter than 0.3 s in the process.
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · Speech, when you have an engine：**If you already have a transcript, pass it.** `transcriptFile` takes SRT, WebVTT,
or JSON (`[{start,end,text}]`, or `{"segments":[…]}` as whisper-family tools emit)
and is tried **before** the subtitle track and before ASR:

```
video_storyboard({"input": "lecture.mp4", "transcriptFile": "lecture.srt"})
```

The B站 case is the one that pays: the captions are already there, and paying for
a download plus a recogniser to re-derive them would be silly.
section: Speech, when you have an engine

text:
dsh-video-vision README · What it cannot do：- **No bundled ASR.** Speech is transcribed only when the file carries a subtitle
  track or when you point `DSH_ASR_CMD` at an engine (above). With neither, you
  still get the audio summary: speech share, loudness, silences, onsets. Long
  windows are chunked, but the model is yours: this package never downloads one.
- **OCR needs one of three engines.** The Windows one (`Windows.Media.Ocr`) is
  built in; `tesseract` on `PATH` is used on Linux and macOS; `DSH_OCR_CMD` points at
  anything else that takes one image and prints lines. With none of the three the
  tool says so — `DSH_OCR_BACKEND=off` forces that answer, and `video_outline` or
  `video_storyboard` still work because neither reads text. A host whose Windows
  engine has no recogniser language (Windows Server, a trimmed install) counts as
  having none: `video_read` returns pictures with the usual note instead of an
  `OCR failed` error. The language is chosen once — `zh-Hans-CN`, then any
  `zh-hans` variant, then English, then whatever the host has.
- **B站 only, and only what it hands out without an account.** A B站 link is
  resolved through the public endpoints, which mean

src/index.js     plugin entry: registers the five tools, resolves binaries
src/tools.js     tool specs (descriptions are prompt-cached, so they are short)
src/pipeline.js  orchestration + analysis cache

dsh-video-vision README · Thanks：The idea this plugin starts from — one contact sheet with burnt-in cell indices,
plus a text index binding cells to timecodes, put together without an image
library — comes from
[SAOS-3624/dsh-video-storyboard](https://github.com/SAOS-3624/dsh-video-storyboard),
whose documentation is the clearest statement of why it works. Thank you.

dsh-video-vision README · Thanks：This is an independent implementation: no code is copied, and detection, cell
budgeting, decoding and composition differ. The three tool names, their argument
shapes and the manifest grammar are kept compatible on purpose, so it can stand
in where that plugin is already installed. See [NOTICE](NOTICE).
